findings.situation: A filer had a 2024 net capital loss, or a loss carried into 2024, but filed no 2024 return or no 2024 Schedule D (or one that left out the carryover), so line 21 showed no loss and the filer truthfully answers no.
findings.source_text: p550 p. 102: "you must take the current year's allowable deduction into account, whether or not you claimed it and whether or not you filed a return for the current year"
findings.why: The carryover depends on what a correct 2024 Schedule D line 21 would have shown, not what was actually filed. The question asks what line 21 'showed', so these filers answer no and lose lines 6 and 14. The clcw notice that warns about this only appears after a yes, so they never see it.

findings.situation: Spouses filed jointly in 2024 and the other spouse had the capital loss; one spouse now files a separate 2025 return and truthfully answers yes because the joint 2024 Schedule D line 21 showed a loss.
findings.source_text: i1040sd p. 10: "If you and your spouse once filed a joint return and are filing separate returns for 2025, any capital loss carryover from the joint return can be deducted only on the return of the spouse who actually had the loss." Question: "Did line 21 of your 2024 Schedule D show a loss?"
findings.why: The question only tells joint 2025 filers how to answer. A separate 2025 filer is not told to answer only for losses they personally had, so the yes brings in a carryover the lines must not have on that return.

locators: p. 10, Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet—Lines 6 and 14, "Use this worksheet to figure your capital loss carryovers from 2024 to 2025 if your 2024 Schedule D, line 21, is a loss", "Otherwise, you don’t have any carryovers"
p. 102, Capital Losses, "you must take the current year's allowable deduction into account, whether or not you claimed it and whether or not you filed a return for the current year"

p. 9, "capital loss carryforwards must be adjusted"; p. 10, Net Gains and Losses Worksheet, line 2(h), "Enter the amount reported on line 2(i) of this worksheet from your prior tax year return calculations"
p. 1, Part I, line 6, "Short-term capital loss carryover. Enter the amount, if any, from line 8 of your Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet in the instructions"
p. 1, Part II, line 14, "Long-term capital loss carryover. Enter the amount, if any, from line 13 of your Capital Loss Carryover Worksheet in the instructions"

findings.situation: A filer receives a Form 1099-DIV in their own name whose box 2a includes capital gain distributions that belong to another person, such as a co-owner of the account, and truthfully totals box 2a as the help instructs.
findings.source_text: Question help: "The total of box 2a of every Form 1099-DIV and substitute statement in your or your spouse's name"; f1099div p. 5, Nominees: "If this form includes amounts belonging to another person, you are considered a nominee recipient. You must file Form 1099-DIV ... for each of the other owners to show their share of the income"
findings.why: The help asks for the full box 2a total of every form in the filer's name and never says to leave out the nominee share. Schedule D line 13 should carry only the filer's own distributions, so the other owners' share is wrongly counted.

findings.situation: A married filer filing a separate return totals box 2a of every Form 1099-DIV in their own name and their spouse's name, as the help instructs.
findings.source_text: Question help: "every Form 1099-DIV and substitute statement in your or your spouse's name"; i1040sd p. 11, Line 13: "See Capital Gain Distributions, earlier" (the line is the filer's own return line)
findings.why: Unlike the gate's help ("On a joint return, answer for you and your spouse together"), this help does not limit the spouse's amounts to a joint return. A filer on a separate return would therefore bring the spouse's distributions onto their own Schedule D line 13.

locators: p. 5, Instructions for Recipient, "Box 2a. Shows total capital gain distributions from a regulated investment company (RIC) or real estate investment trust (REIT)"
